title: Count activation at value received, not setup finished
decision_task: Which event ClimbOS treats as 'activated' when reading the owner's funnel and when running PB-activation-repair.
applies_when: Self-serve software, apps or digital products with signups or trials
The owner reports an 'activated' count or ClimbOS reads product events
Collaborative or team products where value needs more than one person
exclusions: Service businesses where first value is a delivered job, attended session or first order (keep Book 08's business-specific milestones)
Too few signups to compare later outcomes of users who did vs did not reach the event: keep the event as a labelled hypothesis
The owner cannot observe any value event: measure first
required_inputs: A countable value event (publish, send, receive, share, export, deploy type action)
evidence_requirements: Separate counts for setup completed and value received in the same signup cohort
Later paid or retained rate for users who reached each stage vs those who did not
The product's natural use frequency (daily, weekly, monthly, episodic) for the habit stage
missing_data_behavior: Owner reports setup completion as 'activated': label activationKind 'setup' and lower the diagnosis basis to partial.
No observable value event: first step defines and instruments it.
alternatives_when_constrained: Missing data: ask the owner to mark 10–20 recent signups as 'got the result' or not and compare who paid
Low traffic: watch 3–5 new users (PB-activation-repair step) and record where value happens
No integration: weekly manual count from the owner's admin view

decision_branches.then: Use the count in diagnosis as measured.
Diagnosis partial; define the value event first.
Activation may be counted at team level.

implementation_steps: List setup steps separately from value events
Name the value event as the moment the user gets a result, using the verb test
Add a quantity only if the data supports one (her survey example used several responses)
Define habit as repeat use over a window matched to natural frequency, not 'active last week'
Compare paid and retained rates of users who reached setup, value and habit
Choose the earliest stage that clearly separates later payers or retainers
For team products make collaboration part of the activation event and put the invite in setup
dependencies: Event tracking for the value event

cash_and_labor_requirements.tools: Product analytics or a manual count

metrics: Value-event rate within a stated window
Paid and retained rate conditional on each stage
guardrails: Never report setup completion as activation
Pair any activation lift with later retention or paid conversion so empty test activity cannot inflate it
observation_window: Value event within a product-specific window stated up front; validate the definition over at least one full billing or renewal cycle of the cohort.
stop_conditions: Activated users do not pay or retain better than non-activated: definition is wrong, move it
Almost everyone reaches the event: it is setup, move it later
Event cannot be measured reliably: revert to owner-marked sample
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes
climbos_location: shared/agents/diagnosis.ts (OwnerFunnel.activated comment lists 'completed setup'; diagnose() activation vs conversion split); shared/playbooks/contracts.ts PB-activation-repair step 1; owner funnel input UI.

interpretation: INTERPRETATION: Verna's setup/aha/habit split maps onto ClimbOS's activation-vs-conversion branch. Counting setup as activation inflates the activation rate and pushes the computed constraint toward 'conversion', which sends owners to price changes when users never got value.
proposed_climbos_rule: PROPOSED RULE: Change the OwnerFunnel.activated description to 'reached the result (not just finished setup)'. Add activationKind: 'setup' | 'value' | 'habit' | 'unknown'. When it is 'setup' or 'unknown', diagnosis basis drops to 'partial' and the plan's first step must define the value event. Team products may define activation at team level.
disagreements: diagnosis.ts includes 'completed setup' in the activated count, which Verna explicitly rejects. Her subtitle claim that nearly all monetization and retention problems come from activation is rhetoric, not data; do not encode it as a prior.

hypothetical_evaluation_cases.label: hypothetical
expected_behavior: Flags that 150 counts setup, not value
Uses or asks for the value-event count (30) and recomputes: activation 15%, activated-to-paid 40%
Names activation, not conversion, as the binding constraint once the value event is used, and states the diagnosis flips with the definition
First plan step defines and instruments the value event
hard_failure: Accepts 150 as activated without a flag and makes a pricing or checkout change the bankable play
Invents a value-event count the owner did not give

notes: Proposed reference contract. Not executable; does not authorize publishing, sending or spending. Numbers in source references are dated author figures, never forecasts.
